subject: ADR-215: the board printed 'everything is green' beside a reading of 6 / 7, and said nothing about which numbers decide
body: The Harness Board is this kit's one summary artefact and its headline was not derived from what it displays. all_green was a hand-written conjunction over seven summary fields while the page rendered eleven tiles, six of which do not gate the verdict -- one of them reading '6 / 7 clean under load'. A reader with that and 'Everything the harness knows how to check is green' on one screen has to distrust one of the two, and the page gave them nothing to decide with. FOUND BY A READER, NOT AN AUDIT: a subagent republishing the board noticed the two statements side by side and said so. ADR-141's shape at the top of the kit rather than inside a page: a rule kept in one place and published in another, with nothing holding the two together -- the conjunction could be extended without the page ever mentioning it, and a tile could be added without anyone deciding whether it gates. The verdict is now DERIVED from a named list of seven gates and the list is RENDERED, with any unmet gate marked NOT MET. The honest shape is not 'every tile gates': two of the seven have no tile at all -- the walks and the traces -- so the list is named rather than inferred from what happens to be displayed. Every tile then says which it is: four carry 'counts toward the verdict' and the other seven say in one line what kind of number they are instead, and the renderer ASSERTS it -- a tile that neither gates nor has a reason stops the render rather than printing an unexplained ratio. AND THE RULE FIRES: every check would pass on a page whose banner was hard-coded green, so verify_board breaks a gate on a COPY of the ledgers, re-renders, and requires the banner to go red and that gate -- and only that gate -- to be named NOT MET. verify_board 102 to 112.
